name: git-devops-service-principal
description: Azure DevOps credentials for git — run ordinary git commands (clone, fetch, pull, push) against Azure DevOps repositories, authenticated as an Entra service principal.

settings.label: Service principal client ID
settings.description: Application (client) ID of the Entra app registration / service principal that Azure DevOps is accessed as. Public information — it is the id you see on the app registration's overview blade, and it is safe to read back here. The matching secret goes in the credential field below, not here.

settings.label: Entra tenant ID
settings.description: The directory (tenant) GUID the service principal lives in. A client-credentials sign-in is always tenant-specific, so `common` and `organizations` do NOT work here — use the GUID.

settings.label: Azure DevOps organisation
settings.description: The organisation to talk to: a bare name (`contoso`), a modern URL (`https://dev.azure.com/contoso`) or a legacy one (`https://contoso.visualstudio.com`) are all accepted. Used for the sign-in check, and to know which hosts to attach the credential to. A git command carries its own full URL, so both URL styles keep working whichever form is set here.

settings.label: Commit author name
settings.description: Name recorded as the author and committer of commits made through this plugin. Leave empty to inherit the server user's own git identity. Set only for this plugin: it is injected per command and nothing is written to the machine's git configuration.

settings.label: Commit author email
settings.description: Email recorded alongside the name above. Azure DevOps matches a commit to a person by this address, so an address the organisation does not know still commits fine but shows as an unlinked author. Note this wins over a per-repository identity in that clone's own .git/config, because it is injected at the highest precedence git has — which is the point of setting it here, but worth knowing if a checkout has its own identity.

secrets.label: Service principal secret (password)
secrets.description: The client secret / password of that app registration — Certificates & secrets -> New client secret. Write-only: it is encrypted at rest and never read back by any API. Client secrets expire, so if git suddenly reports an authentication failure, check the expiry date before anything else.
